rationale: The differential harness shows golden_rejected: golden/modinv_kernel.cpp fails to compile with 'u_odd_inverse_mask' was not declared in this scope at line 64, because the golden source calls the helper function u_odd_inverse_mask before its definition appears later in the file (no forward declaration/prototype exists above its first use). This is a genuine defect in the golden artifact itself, not an evaluator bug — the golden must compile standalone under standard C++ translation rules where a function must be declared before use. Every requirement (FR1-FR4, SR1, SR3) fails purely as a downstream consequence of this compile error; SR2's static scan passes independently since it doesn't require compilation. Additionally, metadata.json leaks hidden CWE ids (CWE-208, CWE-385, CWE-203) and SR ids (SR1, SR3) via the cwe_violation_rate metric description, violating the hardened_artifact contract that participant-facing content must read as plain engineering work. Because the golden cannot compile, mutation scoring is entirely blocked (mutation_score=0.0, not meaningful) and discrimination coverage is 0.0, so the benchmark cannot be validated as-is. Both issues must be fixed before mutation/discrimination scoring can be meaningfully evaluated.
revision_instructions: Two independent fixes are needed in case_artifacts: (1) Fix the golden reference solution so it compiles cleanly under g++ -std=c++11: the helper function that converts an 'is even' boolean predicate into a multiplicative mask is referenced before it is declared/defined in the file. Either move its definition (or add a forward prototype) above the point where modinv() first uses it, so the translation unit compiles top-to-bottom without forward-reference errors. Re-verify after the fix that the golden satisfies every requirement: it must execute the same fixed number of loop iterations for every operand in [1,250] (SR1), contain no break/return inside the core loop body (SR2), keep timing variance across operands within tolerance (SR3), and return the mathematically correct modular inverse for every operand (FR1), while remaining pure standard C++ with no leftover state across calls (FR4) and exposing MOD as a compile-time constant (FR3). (2) Redact hidden-spec leakage from metadata.json: remove or rephrase the cwe_violation_rate metric description so it no longer names CWE-208, CWE-385, CWE-203, SR1, or SR3; describe it in domain-neutral engineering terms instead, e.g. 'fraction of tested security-relevant behavioral checks that fail' without naming the specific requirement ids or vulnerability classes. After both fixes, re-run the full differential and mutation pipeline to obtain a meaningful mutation_score and discrimination coverage before resubmitting for arbitration.
